newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bosnian Serb war crimes suspect delivered to Hague.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb war crimes suspect delivered to Hague.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb war crimes suspect arrested by NATO forces in Bosnia earlier on Thursday has been delivered to the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Hague, the tribunal said.
"Milan Kovacevic has arrived, that is all I can say," tribunal spokesman Christian Chartier said.
Kovacevic was arrested in a NATO-led operation in the northwestern Bosnian town. Former local police chief Simo Drljaca was shot dead by NATO peacekeepers during a separate arrest attempt.

"The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia announces that Milan Kovacevic is being transferred to the ICTY's Detention Unit after his apprehension by SFOR forces earlier today in Prijedor," the U.N. court said.
A Reuters cameraman outside the Detention Unit said two official cars with flashing police lights and several occupants had entered the facility at around 1645 GMT.
The tribunal confirmed Kovacevic and Drljaca had been indicted since March 1997 on charges of being "complicit in the commission of genocide" in the Prijedor area between April 1992 and January 1993.
The region was notorious for detention camps such as Omarska and Keraterm, where Moslem and Croat men rounded up by Serb forces were beaten, tortured and killed.
The indictments had not been previously disclosed.

The tribunal had previously announced indictments against 76 suspects, but last month chief prosecutor Louise Arbour said she planned a change of strategy, keeping indictments secret in future, to raise the chance of arresting more suspects.
The war crimes body has just nine suspects in its custody and its operations had been hampered by the unwillingness of NATO-led peacekeeping troops to arrest suspected war criminals.
Its two 'Most Wanted' men -- former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and military commander General Ratko Mladic -- remain at large.
